review_evidence: codex self-review: pedagogy, grammar, ambiguity, grading, passage independence, and age fit
title: Seeing without Seeing
source_note: NCERT structural alignment only. Zidd uses original teaching passages, checks, and feedback instead of copying the textbook body.

levels.title: Choose the sense clue
levels.focus: identify whether touch, hearing, smell, or taste gives the clue
levels.teaching_goal: Read a short situation and identify the sense that helps the child learn about an object.

guided_check.teaching_block: A sense clue tells how we learn something. Worked example: a ringing phone gives a hearing clue. Do not choose sight when the passage says the eyes are covered.
guided_check.passage: With her eyes covered, Joya feels a rough shell in her hand.
guided_check.prompt: Which sense helps Joya notice that it is rough?

bridge.teaching_block: Listen for sound words such as buzz, ring, or clap. These point to hearing.
bridge.passage: Arun hears a steady buzz near the flower pot.
bridge.prompt: Which sense gives Arun the clue?

masterclass.teaching_block: A scent reaches the nose. The word “sweet” can describe taste or smell, so use the action “sniffs” to decide.
masterclass.passage: Mili sniffs a sweet scent from a closed box.

independent_check.teaching_block: Name the sense from the action in the passage. Keep the answer to one short phrase.
independent_check.passage: Before eating, Rehan touches a cup and notices that it is warm.
independent_check.prompt: Which sense tells Rehan the cup is warm?

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer sense-clue reading to cooking. The setting changes, but the clue still comes through the nose.
transfer_check.passage: From the doorway, Sana notices the scent of toasted bread.

levels.title: Understand clue words
levels.focus: use context to understand texture, scent, and sound words
levels.teaching_goal: Infer the meaning of a sense word from the action and result around it.

guided_check.teaching_block: Context can explain a new word. Worked example: “The stone scratched my hand; it was rough” shows rough means not smooth.
guided_check.passage: The blanket felt fuzzy. Tiny soft fibres brushed Kavi’s fingers.

bridge.teaching_block: Use the result as a clue. If a sound is faint, someone may move closer to hear it.
bridge.passage: The bell made a faint sound, so Tara stepped nearer to hear it.

masterclass.teaching_block: “Aroma” is explained by the nose and food clue, not by the object’s colour.
masterclass.passage: A warm, spicy aroma came from the soup. Dev noticed it with his nose.

independent_check.teaching_block: Use the touch clues without choices.
independent_check.passage: The wooden block was smooth; Meera’s finger moved over it without catching.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer context reading to a weather sound. The surrounding words explain the new sound word.
transfer_check.passage: A low rumble rolled across the sky before the rain. It sounded like a distant drum.

levels.title: Use sense and access words
levels.focus: use words such as chime, raised dots, texture, and direction correctly
levels.teaching_goal: Choose a chapter word that accurately names a clue, feature, or helpful tool.

guided_check.teaching_block: A “texture” is how a surface feels. Worked example: smooth and bumpy are two textures. It is not the name of the object itself.
guided_check.passage: One card is silky and another is rough.
guided_check.prompt: Which word names the way their surfaces feel?

bridge.teaching_block: Raised dots stand above a flat surface and can be felt. Focus on the touch clue rather than the page colour.
bridge.passage: Nikhil runs his fingertips over dots that stand above the page.

masterclass.teaching_block: A chime is a clear ringing sound. If you chose “direction,” check whether the question asks what was heard or where it came from.
masterclass.passage: A clear ring sounds when the door opens.
masterclass.prompt: Which chapter word names this sound?

independent_check.teaching_block: The passage contains both the target direction and the sound clue. Use them together.
independent_check.passage: A bell rings on Lata’s right side. She turns right towards the bell.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer access-word use to a lift. The raised mark can be found by touch rather than sight.
transfer_check.passage: Inside a lift, Omar feels a raised arrow on one button.

levels.title: Actions and describing clues
levels.focus: distinguish action and describing words in sense sentences
levels.teaching_goal: Find verbs that show sensing actions and adjectives that describe sounds, smells, tastes, or textures.

guided_check.teaching_block: Sensing actions are verbs: touches, hears, sniffs, and tastes. Worked example: in “Mina sniffs the flower,” sniffs is the action.
guided_check.passage: Aarav gently taps the metal cup.

bridge.teaching_block: A describing word tells what a thing is like. “Sharp” describes the sound; “rings” is the action.

masterclass.teaching_block: Match the action to the named person. Another descriptive clue may appear nearby.
masterclass.passage: Nora smells the fresh mint leaf.
masterclass.prompt: Which word tells what Nora does?

independent_check.teaching_block: Find the describing word without choices.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer the word-job test to food preparation. Look for the action done with the ears.
transfer_check.passage: The cook listens for the soft timer bell.

levels.title: Explain a helpful way
levels.focus: write a respectful complete sentence about using a sense clue or offering help
levels.teaching_goal: Write a sentence that names a useful action and respects the other person’s choice and independence.

guided_check.teaching_block: Helpful language says what can be done without assuming a person cannot act. Worked example: “Ask before offering your arm.” is clear and respectful.
guided_check.passage: A classmate is finding the classroom door by touch.
guided_check.prompt: Which sentence is the most respectful?
options: Ask if the classmate would like help.
accepted_answers: Ask if the classmate would like help.
ask if the classmate would like help

bridge.teaching_block: A complete direction needs a landmark or sound. “Go there” is unclear because it gives no usable clue.
bridge.passage: A soft drum is sounding near the reading corner.
bridge.prompt: Which direction is clear and complete?
options: Walk towards the drum sound near the reading corner.
accepted_answers: Walk towards the drum sound near the reading corner.
walk towards the drum sound near the reading corner

masterclass.teaching_block: Choose an action that increases access. Moving an obstacle is more useful than describing its colour.
masterclass.passage: A school bag blocks the clear path to the desk.
options: Move the bag away from the path.
accepted_answers: Move the bag away from the path.
move the bag away from the path

independent_check.teaching_block: Write one respectful sentence. Include asking first and the kind of help that could be offered.
independent_check.passage: Viren is listening for his group near a noisy doorway.
independent_check.prompt: Write what a classmate could say or do to offer help respectfully.

concept_slots.description: Offers a useful clue or guidance.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer respectful support to a museum visit. Offer access to information without taking over.
transfer_check.passage: A visitor wants to learn about a model by touch, but the display has a “staff assistance” sign.
transfer_check.prompt: Write one complete sentence suggesting a respectful next step.

items.passage: Pavi hears a whistle from the playground.
items.prompt: Which sense gives Pavi the clue?

items.passage: With eyes closed, Yana feels a cool marble in her palm.
items.prompt: How does Yana notice the marble is cool?

items.passage: A fresh orange scent comes from the lunch box.
items.prompt: Which sense can notice the scent?

items.passage: Raghu tastes one tiny drop of safe lemon water and notices it is sour.
items.prompt: Which sense tells Raghu it is sour?

items.passage: The towel was damp, with a little water still in it.
The perfume had a strong scent that reached the hallway.
The alarm gave a piercing beep that made everyone cover their ears.
The cushion felt springy and rose again after Mina pressed it.
accepted_answers: soft and able to spring back

items.passage: A surface has many tiny bumps.
items.prompt: Which word names how the surface feels?

items.passage: Dots stand above a flat card and can be felt with a finger.
A clear ringing note comes from a hanging metal tube.
The guide says, “The doorway is on your left,” and taps once beside the left wall.
Tina sniffs the warm soup.
A low drum beats slowly.
items.prompt: Which word describes the drum sound?

items.passage: Kabir touches the silky ribbon.
The child listens beside the open window.
A chair blocks the walking path.
options: Move the chair out of the path.
accepted_answers: Move the chair out of the path.
move the chair out of the path

items.passage: A classmate is searching for the correct desk.
options: Would you like me to describe where it is?
accepted_answers: Would you like me to describe where it is?
would you like me to describe where it is

items.passage: The exit bell sounds beside the main door.
items.prompt: Which sentence gives a clear clue?
options: The main door is beside the exit bell.
accepted_answers: The main door is beside the exit bell.
the main door is beside the exit bell

items.passage: A visitor asks how to reach the quiet reading room. A soft music player is outside its door.
items.prompt: Write one complete sentence giving a useful direction.

concept_slots.description: Names the reading room or its door.
Uses the soft music as the landmark.
Connects the room to the landmark.
